# `Q-11-1` — Lua Filter Diagnostic

> A Lua filter emitted a diagnostic message during execution.

## What this means

Quarto supports Lua filters — small Lua programs that
transform the document AST between parsing and rendering. A
filter can emit diagnostics of its own through Quarto's filter
API: warnings the user should see, errors that abort the run.
Every such diagnostic surfaces with code `Q-11-1`. The
underlying filter is the source of the message.

This single code covers every filter-emitted diagnostic
because the meaning is determined by the filter, not by
Quarto. The accompanying message and (when available) source
location come from the filter author.

## Why this happens

The trigger is entirely filter-specific. Common patterns:

- **Input the filter could not process** — a node shape the
  filter did not anticipate.
- **A precondition violation** — a metadata key the filter
  expected to find was missing.
- **A deliberate authoring constraint** — the filter checks
  the document against a project-specific style rule and
  reports violations.

## How to fix

Read the filter's message — it is the authoritative source for
what to do. If the filter does not document its diagnostics,
the filter's source code (`.lua` file) is the next place to
look.

## Related

There are no other `Q-11-*` codes. Quarto-side filter problems
that are not the filter's own diagnostics surface under
different codes (often `Q-0-1` for internal failures inside
the filter runtime).
